title.narrative: Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity and resilience of labour administrations

description.narrative:
In 2022, Ministry of Labour and Social Security (MLSS) improved data collection and retrieval capabilities through the introduction and use of handheld tablets and digital forms by labour officers and inspectors in the MLSS. The use of technology also assisted the Ministry’s streamlining of the processes for labour inspections on Occupational Safety and Health (OSH), child labour (CL) and other areas of labour administration, reducing the time required for each exercise and time previously spent preparing written/paper-based reports. These incremental improvements also contributed to the rate and quality of compliance interventions.
In 2022 and 2023, the MLSS also enhanced the capacity of labour officers, OSH inspectors and social workers to plan for and conduct CL inspections. As the Ministry has increasingly adopted a ‘strategic compliance planning’ approach, 60 officers across various specialized areas were trained to undertake “general compliance” inspections. This allows more efficient use of existing personnel to meet nationwide delivery of services. Additionally, as the information gathered in inspections is now digitalized, the resulting improvement in availability and access to information supports the generation of more detailed and comprehensive reports, and better analyses that are being used to inform strategic planning and guide the efficient deployment of personnel and other resources for child labour inspections and other functions of the Ministry.
Jamaica also realized an increased capacity of National Steering Committee on Child Labour (NASTOCL) representatives to develop Operational plans in 2022. As an example of the strategic approach adopted, the Ministry (Chair of the NASTOCL) has also used Child Labour Risk Identification maps which provide geographic information on the relative prevalence of risk/vulnerability factors. In February 2022, building on previous ILO support for digitalization of inspections and other services at the Ministry of Labour and Social Security, the ILO facilitated through an RBSA project, the procurement of 10 additional handheld tablets with necessary accessories and software in this biennium for distribution to labour officers. This was complemented by ILO grant funding and technical support for execution of four (4) capacity building workshops, the first two in February and March of 2022, and then in February and March of 2023 on use of the data processing equipment and on conduct of inspections using a revised “general compliance inspection” approach for labour officers and inspectors.
The in-house training targeted labour officers in various units (Occupational Safety and Health, Child Labour Unit, Industrial Relations, Pay and Conditions of Employment, Employment Agencies Unit etc.) and in field offices across Jamaica. It provided instruction in using the digital tools and in the “revised general compliance inspection” procedure, which was developed with the aim of reducing the number of separate/ specialised inspections being done by different departments of the Ministry. This change in procedure also enabled the Ministry to ensure the inclusion of child labour among the issues considered in inspections.
In April 2022, an ILO-led workshop for inter-ministerial and tripartite representatives of the National Steering Committee on Child Labour (NASTOCL) presented updated child labour risk maps for Jamaica and examined the requirements for CLRISK Phase 2- the use of risk maps and analysis in decision-making and local policy and programme development. This supported Jamaica’s “phase 2” application of the Child Labour Risk Identification Model (CLRISK), through building capacity to use innovative information to guide implementation planning and programme design.
